questions.text: What defines centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) in multi-agent RL?

options.A: A joint critic can use global state and actions during training, while each deployed policy uses its local observation.
options.B: Every agent shares one action at execution, while each critic trains only on its agent’s local observation.
options.C: Agents train and deploy with full global state, while their rewards remain private during execution.
options.D: One central policy selects all agents’ actions at execution, while each agent trains its own local critic.

questions.explanation: CTDE gives the training critic joint information to handle coordination, but each agent’s deployed policy acts from its own local observation.

questions.text: In a competitive game, a single agent repeatedly trains against its latest copy and cycles among strategies that beat one another. Which training change best addresses this?

options.A: Use only the most recent opponent policy so updates remain on-policy.
options.B: Remove opponent history and increase the discount factor instead.
options.C: Train against a league containing past and varied opponent policies.
options.D: Give every opponent the same action so the game becomes stationary.

questions.explanation: League play samples from a population of past and varied opponents, which helps expose and reduce cyclic weaknesses that single-opponent self-play can miss.

questions.text: In CoopGridWorld.step, done is true only when both new positions equal (5,5); reward is 10 if done, otherwise -1. If the two new positions are ((5,5),(5,4)), what does step report for reward and done?
questions.explanation: Only one agent has reached the shared goal, so the conjunction is false; the environment returns the per-step penalty -1 and done=False.
